name: background-beams

frames.best_why: Frame 4 catches the most beams at once, spread across the upper and lower halves of the panel.

tagline: Faint cyan and violet threads drift down behind a dark waitlist panel.
summary: A dark backdrop of long curved lines along which short cyan-to-violet gradient segments travel downward on staggered loops. It is meant to sit behind a headline, some copy and an email field.
appearance: A near-black panel with a large pale gradient headline, a block of grey paragraph text and a dark rounded email field holding a grey placeholder. Thin coloured threads in cyan, indigo and violet curve down across the empty space around them.
behaviour: Short gradient segments run along long fixed curves, each on its own six-to-twelve second loop with a random start, so a few beams are always sliding downward and fading at either end. Nothing reacts to the pointer.
demo_content: Headline "Join the waitlist", a MailJet email-service paragraph and a you@company.com email field.
search_phrases: thin glowing lines falling down a page
light trails drifting in the backdrop
colourful streaks behind a signup form
subtle particle beams for a hero
animated curves of light behind text
waitlist page with moving laser lines
use_when: A dark waitlist or hero panel needs faint motion behind centred copy and a field.
avoid_when: You need a punchy or high-contrast effect: the beams nearly vanish on most screens.
customise: Only className is exposed. The fifty hardcoded path shapes, their cyan-purple stops and the random loop timings are baked into the file.
weight_why: Roughly fifty SVG paths, each animating its own gradient coordinates forever.

a11y.note: The decorative SVG is not marked aria-hidden and the endless loops have no reduced-motion check.

issues: The beams are faint and sparse, so most of the panel stays as flat black.
polish_why: A restrained, competent effect, but the threads are so dim that the panel reads almost static.
title: Background Beams
